title: Kanban swimlanes: row counts and per-cell figures are page floors on a windowed board; read them whole with one grouped query
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA

Filing gate: ① (split from #37718 item N5: a read-path behaviour change, not a wording fix) · Source: fleet (contract review 7205497529 on PR #37714)

## What happens

On a self-querying kanban that reads its records a page at a time and lays them out in swimlanes, each swimlane's row count and each cell's figure are computed from the rows loaded so far. They are floors, not totals: a board whose later pages hold more records shows smaller numbers than the data has. The flat board already reads whole column counts when the list hands over one page (PR #37714); the swimlane layout does not.

## Expected

On a windowed swimlane board, the row counts and per-cell figures come from one grouped read on both keys (lane field × swimlane field), pushed down to SQL, so they are whole whatever page is loaded. Where the data source cannot group, the figures stay as today and say they are partial.

## Done when

- [ ] One two-key grouped read feeds the swimlane row counts and cell figures on a windowed board.
- [ ] A test pins whole figures with a second page not yet loaded, and a control where the source cannot group.
- [ ] No extra read on a board that already holds every record.

Grade: area:ux · Feature · reach: a swimlane kanban over more records than one page · evidence: read (the review of PR #37714), not measured
Suggested-grade: p3
Size: S–M
